what_this_is: W21b residue (C13): same-topic / same-level forward references that no unlock move could fix, rewritten in lesson prose (a <sentence> card becomes a glossed plain line, or a decorative card is dropped); the exercise cites of the same sentence are emptied.
fold_rule: verdict keyed by the row's stable identity: ok -> the authored text; corrected -> the verifier's text (authored text kept as authored_*); rejected -> `held`, never applied
apply_contract: per lesson, in table order, per span: body.count(from) == count, then body = body.replace(from, to). A span whose `from` is gone (and whose `to` is present, when non-empty) is already applied. Both layers: research/derived/lessons/<slug>.json body and localized_text(lesson, body, pt-BR).

authored_header.method:
Residue listed by running the gating validator's C5 logic (derive_needs.lesson_references over the exported course, introducer = first lesson whose unlocks carry the ref) on the tree at HEAD f34ef379+97550c2a: 1 same-topic + 14 same-level (lesson, item) uses, matching the frozen baseline. Every use comes from a (body card, and for 8 rows also exercise sentence_refs); none from a chip or a reading. For each row the bank was searched for a replacement sentence whose every introduced ref is unlocked at or before the lesson (by grammar tag and by surface pattern); none fit without rewriting the surrounding prose, so no row is a swap. Decorative uses (trailing 'Mais exemplos' cards, supporting cards the prose already covers) are dropped, with a heading that would be left empty. Where the item is essential to the example, the card becomes a plain

... line with the sentence's own pt-BR translation and, where the surrounding prose does not already gloss the item, an inline gloss. Raw is text, not a reference (derive_needs measures it as an annex channel that C5 does not count). Cost of a gloss row: the card loses its tap-to-dissect tokens and audio. Exercise sentence_refs that cite the same sentence are provenance only (validate_sentence_manifest rule 4 is retired); they are emptied. Lesson sentence_refs is derived from the body at export, so it is not edited. Proof (scratch build.py): every old_span occurs exactly once in both the HEAD source body (research/derived/lessons/.json) and the exported body, every exercise edit matches its current value, and applying all rows in memory drops C5 same-topic/same-level to 0/0 with zero new forward uses in any tier (cross-level 160 -> 152 as a side effect: the removed cards also carried 8 cross-level refs). 12 rows are table-locked items (何/なに, なん, どちら, 彼, たび); `alternative` names the address/homograph ruling that would fix them without touching prose. Apply must re-run validate_practice_coverage (exercise cites feed its target surfaces) and lower the C5 baseline with --write-baseline.

verdict_summary.key: lesson + '|' + the row's primary old_span, verbatim
verdict_summary.note: Every old_span (and each 'also' span) occurs exactly once in both the HEAD source (research/derived/lessons) and the HEAD export, and all 11 exercise edits match current values in both. Replaying all 15 rows on a HEAD fixture confirms C5 same-topic/same-level 1/14 -> 0/0 and cross-level 160 -> 152, with no markup errors. The same replay shows two consequences the method does not mention: (1) validate_practice_coverage FAILS with 6 new absents (desu-wa-03 もの/ない; perguntas-06 gp-48/食/食べる/いい), all caused by emptying exercise cites in rows 2, 6 and 7; (2) C4 FAILS 3x until needs[] is re-derived (perguntas-06, particulas-lugar-03, desu-wa-03 note). Several unlocks that W21b moved to these lessons as 'first user' lose that user (rows 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, 8).
